thread:
anya (finance): MeterMesh follow-up — went through their pricing deck and the SKU table is confusing. It mixes per-API-call, per-embedding, and 'token-equivalent' columns. Can procurement/eng confirm what we should ask them before the PO?
matt (procurement): I flagged this in the proposal: line items 2.1 vs 2.3 look like double-charges for inference + telemetry. Need a clean mapping to our usage: generation tokens, embeddings, and ingress events.
kevin (eng-ml): Quick question — does MeterMesh meter at the request boundary or per-token? Their docs say 'billing is per request and per sequence', which is ambiguous for streaming. Can you paste the SKU table?
anya (finance): Paste below (redacted):
```
SKU,Unit,Price
GEN-TOK,token,0.0006
EMB-UNIT,embedding,0.0025
REQ,request,0.0001
SEQ,sequence,per-sequence
```
They also have a note: "sequence pricing may apply to streaming sessions".
kevin (eng-ml): Ugh. That could double-bill streaming where tokens+sequence both apply. We should ask for clarified examples: simple completion, streaming chat, and batch embed file.
lia (legal): Also check contract clause on usage reconciliation windows and invoice dispute time (they listed 10 days which is short). Need standard 30-day dispute window and a right to audit usage logs.
olivia (security): MeterMesh says they store telemetry for 90 days by default. We need to confirm PII handling and that logs do not contain prompt text by default. Do they support redaction or KMS for logs?
matt (procurement): Action items I can send to the AE: 1) canonical SKU mapping against our three consumption patterns (generation streaming, non-streaming, and embeddings), 2) clear examples with math, 3) invoice timing and dispute window to 30 days, 4) SOC2 + data residency confirmation, 5) SSO/SAML and SCIM support for account access.
anya (finance): Please add question about overage handling and proration for mid-month plan changes. And whether reserved bundles (committed usage) are priced as discounts or as caps.
kevin (eng-ml): For engineering: ask if they expose raw usage exports (CSV/BigQuery) with per-request ids and token counts. We need that for end-of-month reconciliation automation. Example CSV columns I'd want: request_id, timestamp, model, token_in, token_out, embedding_units, customer_id
meter-mesh-bot: New message from MeterMesh AE: "Happy to provide examples — attaching sample invoice and CSV export. SOC2 Type II and SAML supported. Sequence pricing applies only when streaming flag=true; we can disable sequence billing for customers on committed plans."
matt (procurement): Great, I'll consolidate and reply. Anyone want to add priority flags? I'd mark SKU mapping + raw exports + SOC2 as high. Others medium.
anya (finance): Agreed. High: SKU mapping & raw exports; Medium: dispute window & overage rules; Low: residency details (we can escalate later).
kevin (eng-ml): I'll draft what our CSV export schema must include and ping them in the thread.
lia (legal): I'll prepare the audit and dispute language we want to propose in redline.
anya (finance): Thanks — please ping me once you have the consolidated list and I'll approve sending it to AE. :thumbsup:
